surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Palmieri has two goals as the Islanders get past the Canucks
paras: Kyle Palmieri opened the scoring for the Islanders midway through the first, and Matias Maccelli scored his first goal for the Islanders 53 seconds later to make it 2-0. Max Sasson got the Canucks on the board early in the second. Brock Boeser tied it up on the power play late in the period, but the Canucks didn’t score again. Palmieri struck again early in the third to put the Isles ahead for good. Matthew Kessel made his Islanders debut, after four seasons with the Blues, and picked up an assist.

The Islanders outshot the Canucks 38-26, but the Canucks’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Ilya Sorokin made 24 saves for the Islanders, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 35 of 38 at the other end. The Islanders improved to 3-3-0 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Canucks fell to 2-6-0, sixth in the Pacific.
